case_name: Shane Roy Needham v. Janet Lea Needham

issues.label: Appellate standard of review
issues.why: The court must identify the correct standards (abuse of discretion, substantial evidence, legal error) for each challenged ruling.

issues.label: Scope of reserved jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm the magistrate properly retained and later exercised jurisdiction to divide the Alturas shares after the divorce decree.

issues.label: Characterization of Alturas shares
issues.why: The court must ensure the shares were correctly treated as community property (and whether any separate component exists).

issues.label: Characterization of post-decree dividends
issues.why: The court must determine how dividends paid after the decree but before final division are characterized and accounted for in the property division.

issues.label: Proper valuation date
issues.why: The court must decide whether shares should be valued at date of divorce, trial, or another equitable date given post-decree appreciation.

issues.label: Need for valuation finding
issues.why: The court must decide whether Idaho law required a fair market valuation finding before choosing an in-kind division.

issues.label: Unequal division claim
issues.why: The court must assess whether the in-kind division effectively created an unequal distribution (e.g., via control premium/voting power effects).

issues.label: Control premium and voting power
issues.why: The court must consider whether splitting a 50% block into two 25% blocks materially alters value and whether that must be equalized.

issues.label: Marketability/minority discounts
issues.why: The court must consider whether minority status and lack of marketability affect the value of the shares awarded to each party.

issues.label: Equitable division factors
issues.why: The court must apply Idaho Code § 32-712 factors and determine whether findings support the chosen method of division.

issues.label: Disentanglement of spouses
issues.why: The court must consider whether the division minimizes ongoing financial/operational entanglement and whether the court misapplied that consideration.

issues.label: Corporate deadlock rationale
issues.why: The court must assess whether using the divorce decree to resolve corporate governance deadlock is a proper consideration under § 32-712.

issues.label: Best interests of corporation
issues.why: The court must consider whether the magistrate improperly prioritized corporate success over equitable division between spouses.

issues.label: Authority to order in-kind transfer
issues.why: The court must determine whether the divorce court had authority to award shares in-kind rather than order a buyout.

issues.label: Authority to compel document execution
issues.why: The court must determine whether the court could compel Mr. Needham to sign transfer-related documents under its equitable powers.

issues.label: Effect of Buy-Sell Agreement
issues.why: The court must interpret whether a court-ordered transfer to an ex-spouse constitutes a transfer triggering the BSA’s purchase right/obligation.

issues.label: BSA involuntary transfer clause
issues.why: The court must decide whether the decree is a 'court decree/operation of law' transfer covered by BSA § 2(b).

issues.label: Validity of spouse assent to BSA
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether Ms. Needham’s notarized acknowledgment binds her and what rights it creates or waives.

issues.label: Enforceability of BSA against community
issues.why: The court must consider whether the BSA can limit or dictate division of community property in a divorce proceeding.

issues.label: Can court override BSA terms
issues.why: The court must decide whether equitable divorce powers permit ordering a result inconsistent with contractual buy-sell restrictions.

issues.label: Necessity of BSA Waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether a waiver was legally required to transfer shares to Ms. Needham without triggering repurchase at book value.

issues.label: Power to force waiver signatures
issues.why: The court must address whether the court can compel Mr. Needham to consent to a waiver that other shareholders and the corporation must also execute.

issues.label: Waiver as amendment vs. consent
issues.why: The court must decide whether the BSA Waiver materially amends the BSA (requiring contract formalities/consideration) or is merely a permitted consent.

issues.label: Consideration for BSA Waiver
issues.why: If treated as a contract modification, the court must consider whether consideration and mutual assent are present.

issues.label: Third-party rights and due process
issues.why: The court must consider whether ordering actions affecting Alturas/other shareholders implicates rights of nonparties not before the divorce court.

issues.label: Corporate authority to execute waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether Alturas’s president/board/shareholders validly approved the waiver and whether proper corporate procedures were followed.

issues.label: Shareholder consent requirements
issues.why: The court must interpret the BSA/waiver to determine whose signatures are required and the effect of Mr. Needham’s refusal.

issues.label: Specific performance feasibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether it is equitable/possible to specifically enforce an order requiring execution of a waiver when consent is disputed.

issues.label: Alternative remedy if no waiver
issues.why: The court must consider what remedy applies if the BSA cannot be waived (e.g., forced buyout under BSA, monetary equalization, trust/constructive trust).

issues.label: Installment buyout authority
issues.why: The court must decide whether it had discretion to deny an installment buyout and what standards govern installment payment plans.

issues.label: Security for deferred payments
issues.why: If a buyout is ordered, the court must consider the need for interest, security, and enforcement mechanisms to protect the recipient spouse.

issues.label: Trust holding proposal
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether holding shares in trust for Ms. Needham is permissible, practical, and consistent with the BSA and equitable division.

issues.label: Liquidity and tax consequences
issues.why: The court must consider tax and liquidity impacts of dividends, buyout payments, or forced redemption on each spouse’s net distribution.

issues.label: Double-counting dividends/appreciation
issues.why: The court must ensure dividends already shared and appreciation considerations are not counted twice in achieving an equal division.

issues.label: Waste or dissipation claims
issues.why: The court must consider whether either spouse’s conduct (misconduct allegations, competition) affects equitable distribution or valuation adjustments.

issues.label: Fiduciary duties in divorce context
issues.why: The court must consider any fiduciary duties between spouses regarding management of community assets pending final division.

issues.label: Impact on board seat/directorship
issues.why: The court must consider whether transfer affects Mr. Needham’s corporate governance rights and whether that is a cognizable harm in property division.

issues.label: Findings supported by evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether the magistrate’s findings (deadlock, value increase, equity) are supported by substantial and competent evidence.

issues.label: Reliance on Josephson/Lamm
issues.why: The court must determine whether the lower courts correctly applied or distinguished precedent regarding division of closely held stock.

issues.label: Book value vs fair market value
issues.why: The court must address the legal relevance of book value (BSA price) versus fair market value (equitable division) and which controls in context.

issues.label: Public policy on restraints on alienation
issues.why: The court must consider whether enforcing the BSA in divorce implicates policy limits on share-transfer restraints.

issues.label: Remand instructions if error
issues.why: If any abuse of discretion/legal error is found, the court must determine the appropriate remedy (valuation, redivision, buyout, or reconsideration).

issues.label: District court appellate role
issues.why: The court must ensure the district court properly acted as an intermediate appellate court reviewing the magistrate rather than fact-finding anew.

issues.label: Attorney fees on intermediate appeal
issues.why: The court must assess whether the district court correctly found the appeal frivolous/unreasonable and applied the correct fee statute/rule.

issues.label: Attorney fees on further appeal
issues.why: The court must determine entitlement to appellate attorney fees and the governing standard (frivolousness/statutory discretion).

issues.label: Preservation of issues
issues.why: The court must decide which arguments were preserved below (valuation date, BSA effects, waiver authority) and which are waived.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: Even if error occurred, the court must determine whether it affected the outcome of the property division or fees award.
